```json
{"claims":[{"claim_text":"Disparities in health and health care based upon race, ethnicity, socio-economic status, or geography are unacceptable.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Historically, African Americans, Hispanics, Asian Americans, Pacific Islanders, American Indians, and Alaska Natives have experienced poorer health outcomes and received lower-quality care than the majority of Americans.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Infant mortality rates are twice as high among African Americans as whites.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"African American children are twice as likely to have asthma and six times as likely to die from asthma as white children.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The prevalence of HIV/AIDS in Latino populations is four times higher than among whites.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The prevalence of HIV/AIDS among African Americans is nine times higher than that of whites.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Hispanics are nearly twice as likely to die from diabetes as whites.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"African American adults are almost twice as likely to die from heart disease as whites.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"People living in rural and other non-metropolitan areas, regardless of their race or ethnicity, are more likely to experience access problems and poorer health outcomes.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Republicans are committed to addressing these health and health care disparities.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
